A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching models, experiments, and Appendices A–F. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable, and relocated or reformatted material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original lexical-decision, surprisal, anti-surprisal, and BLiMP evaluations, including trained Llama models, learning trajectories, and correlation analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results in Table 1 and the appendices, including training losses, checkpoint evaluations, correlations, and BLiMP scores.

M1.justification: The character/BPE Llama architectures and probability-based word/non-word comparisons remain unchanged. Expanded explanations and newly disclosed evaluation details do not establish a different model, objective, or procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same BabyLM/Pile training coverage, high- and low-frequency Wuggy stimuli, OpenSubtitles contexts, and BLiMP tasks. Newly discussed phonetic resources and multimodal applications are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 4 retain the same six Llama, six Pythia, and two GPT-2 variants. The learning-trajectory comparisons also retain their original membership, excluding GPT-2 because checkpoints are unavailable.

E3.justification: Sample counts, frequency thresholds, model configurations, token-averaged scoring, and the 19-checkpoint schedule are retained. V2 newly specifies beginning-of-sequence tokens and an anti-surprisal insertion index of at least 3, but does not identify these as changes to the existing evaluation.

E4.justification: The tokenization diagnostics, full learning curves, lexical–syntactic correlations, and word/non-word score-difference analyses were already present in Appendices B–F. Revised plotting and merging the frequency-specific figures do not add an analytical question or experiment.

E5.justification: Appendix D retains the same Spearman correlation procedure and statement that all scores satisfy p < 0.05. Neither version adds run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or additional statistical tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1, 3, and 4 match. For example, high-frequency lexical-decision accuracy remains 97.6% for the smallest character Llama and 70.9% for its BPE counterpart. The appendix findings are retained; reformatted plots do not establish new outcomes.

T1.justification: The conditional negative-log-probability comparisons remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version introduces additional formal theory, derivations, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The main character-model advantage and lexical-versus-syntactic timing claims remain. However, the conclusion changes token splitting preempting word learning from an assertion to a plausible explanation involving word discovery, and the abstract explicitly limits the proposed character-model alternative to studying processes below syntax.

C2.justification: The expanded Discussion distinguishes word-form knowledge from contextual word use, acknowledges that human lexical and syntactic learning should overlap, and proposes additional within-word context as an explanation for character-model performance. V2 also adds an argument about how an ideal model should rank ill-fitting real words versus non-words. These substantially develop the interpretation of unchanged results.

D1.justification: V2 documents beginning-of-sequence tokens, the minimum anti-surprisal insertion position, and the one- or two-syllable stimulus differences. Appendices A and B replace anonymized placeholders with explicit model/checkpoint and dataset links. Hardware, training times, and Table 2 hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning through human word-recognition, reference-learning, and mental-lexicon literature, and connects the findings to character-perturbation and letter-counting research. It also revises descriptions of earlier model studies and removes the statement that the cited lexical-decision studies report no learning trajectories.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially revised through expanded related work, rewritten experimental explanations, and a much fuller Discussion. The former Models section is incorporated into Experiments, while the combined Discussion and conclusion becomes separate sections. These changes materially reorganize and explain the paper.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with an expanded caption. Figure 2 replaces smooth curves with checkpoint-by-checkpoint lines and explicit checkpoint ticks. The correlation heatmap is enlarged, and v1 Figures 7–8 become v2 Figure 7(a–b). Table 1 consolidates percentage notation in its caption. These are focused revisions to existing displays.

improvement.justification: V2 better explains what lexical decision measures and qualifies its developmental interpretation, particularly by acknowledging overlap in human lexical and syntactic learning. Added implementation details, explicit artifact links, and clearer checkpoint plots improve transparency. These provide a limited overall quality gain while preserving the original empirical evidence and central argument.
